 Order

This application for anticipatory bail under Section 438 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioner, in connection with FIR No.103/2018 registered at Police Station Deogarh, District Rajsamand, for offences under Sections 420 and 406 IPC.

As per prosecution, a scheme was launched by the Department of Medical Health Services,
Government of Rajasthan to provide free of cost services to expecting pregnant women, for cesarean operation.

entities.text:
Department of Medical Health Services,
Government of Rajasthan
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The petitioner is director of Stuti Hospital, Rajsamand which was one of the private hospitals selected to provide services in the aforementioned scheme.
As per the scheme, on each cesarean operation undertaken by the hospital, the Government would compensate the hospital by making payment of Rs.10,000.

The allegation against Stuti Hospital of which the petitioner is director, is that in contravention of the terms and conditions of the scheme, they charged fee from the (2 of 3) [CRLMB-2723/2022] patients for cesarean operations and have also taken the payment in form of compensation from the Government, thereby cheated the public and caused financial loss to the public exchequer.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner has been implicated in a false case.
Learned counsel submitted that the FIR against the petitioner was lodged in the year 2018 therefore, no fruitful purpose will be served by sending him behind the bars after a period of five years.

Learned counsel further submitted that this Court vide order dated 18.05.2022 granted Sanjay Gupta vs State Of Rajasthan on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112059333/
1 interim protection to the petitioner from arrest subject to his joining the investigation.

sentences.text: Learned counsel submitted that in compliance of the order dated 18.05.2022, the petitioner has already joined the investigation and has appeared before Investigating Officer as and when directed by him.
Learned counsel further submitted that all relevant documents required for investigation have already been furnished by the petitioner to the Investigating Officer.

Learned counsel submitted that in the present facts and circumstances of the case, custodial interrogation of the petitioner is not at all necessitated, particularly when he has fully co-operated with the investigating agency.
Learned counsel thus, prayed that the petitioner may be granted anticipatory bail.
Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor opposed the bail application.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Public Prosecutor.
Perused the material available on record.

Having considered the rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case and upon a consideration of the (3 of 3) [CRLMB-2723/2022] arguments advanced at bar, this Court is of the opinion that after about five years of the lodging of the FIR, it would not be justified to send the petitioner behind bars, when he has already appeared and cooperated with the investigating agency.
Thus, this Court is of the view that it is a fit case for grant of anticipatory bail to the petitioner under Section 438 Cr.P.C.

Accordingly, the bail application under Section 438 Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is ordered that in the event of arrest of the petitioner- Sanjay Gupta S/o Omprakash Gupta in connection with FIR No.103/2018 registered at Police Station Deogarh, District Rajsamand, the petitioner shall be released on bail; provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the concerned investigating officer/S.H.O. on the following conditions:
(i). that the petitioner shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required;
(ii). that the petitioner shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or any police officer; and (iii). that the petitioner shall not leave India without previous permission of the court.
